units.function: Database-backed tests for plugin-declared managed Agents: create/resolve by stable resource key, preserve or reset human edits, select a prevalent compatible adapter, generate path-aware instructions, repair bindings and optionally create a hire approval.
units.dependencyDirection: A plugin manifest with agents.managed capability enters host services; host services materialize first-class Agent/config revision/approval rows, plugin resource/entity bindings and instruction files using Company settings/local folders. Plugin authority therefore crosses directly into organizational principal and executable runtime state.
units.keyDataModels: Plugin manifest/capability/Agent declaration; Agent role/title/capabilities/adapter/config/runtime/permissions/budget; Company approval policy; plugin-managed resource/entity binding and metadata marker; instruction template/local folder path; hire_agent approval payload.
units.lifecycle: Reconcile a stable plugin resource key into an Agent; preserve subsequent edits; explicitly reset to manifest; choose an installed fleet adapter; materialize instructions; relink an orphaned metadata marker; optionally leave the created Agent pending board approval.
units.testAssessment: The six scenarios provide useful lifecycle ideas—stable resource keys, non-destructive reconcile, explicit reset, same-Company relink and optional pending approval—but all were skipped locally because embedded Postgres was unavailable. Critical boundaries are missing: negative capability/tenant authorization, signed manifest provenance, concurrent reconcile uniqueness, tampered/duplicate markers, safe update/security-patch policy, reset authorization, approval accept/reject effects, uninstall/orphan/disable behavior, audit records and rollback. Adapter choice is based on fleet popularity rather than verified health/credential/config fit, and generated instructions expose absolute host paths.
units.designRationale: Allow plugins to ship ready-made specialized Agents that can be installed repeatedly without overwriting user customization, while supporting a Company policy that asks the board to approve new Agents.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must let Connectors/templates propose reusable Agent roles without allowing extension code to create organizational principals, executable commands, permissions or budgets outside a real human responsibility contract.
units.companyOsFit: REJECT plugin-authoritative Agent creation/reset. Keep only the stable resource-key and declarative proposal concepts. A signed extension may submit an AgentRoleProposal containing complete immutable hashes for connector/package, role, capabilities, executable/model profile, permission/data requests, budget, reporting line and instructions. A qualified human must accept a ResponsibilityContract and exact proposal digest before Company OS creates/binds a Principal. Reconcile must be three-way/versioned, security updates explicit, reset a reviewed change, and uninstall suspend rather than delete until ownership/evidence/data retention is resolved. Adapter selection must use declared capabilities, health, locality and secret availability, never fleet popularity alone.
units.responsibilityConflict: With approval disabled by default, a plugin can directly instantiate an Agent with executable command, permissions and budget. Even the optional approval omits accountable human, reporting owner, responsibility contract and full configuration/action digest. This conflicts directly with Company OS's premise that an Agent cannot assume organizational responsibility and every Agent role must have a real responsible human.

units.securityFindings: CRITICAL authority escalation: a plugin manifest can create an executable Agent principal with permissions and budget when optional board approval is off. CRITICAL approval-binding gap: pending hire approval does not bind the full immutable Agent/connector/permission/budget/responsibility digest. HIGH code-execution risk: manifest adapterConfig contains an executable process command and explicit reset can restore it over user edits. HIGH ownership risk: relink trusts editable Agent metadata without conflict/tamper proof. HIGH host-disclosure risk: generated Agent instructions contain absolute local folder paths. HIGH lifecycle gap: plugin upgrade/disable/uninstall, orphan suspension, security updates and evidence retention are untested. MEDIUM adapter-selection risk: fleet popularity can choose a runtime without proving credentials, health, locality or semantic compatibility. TEST GAP: all database-backed scenarios were skipped locally.
